Name: Muse Restaurant & Wine Bar
Description: Mediterranean cooking, pasta and wine in a small historic house. The most convenient sit-down dinner in this guide: next door to your lodging.
Planning notes: Reserve for dinner; check Sunday service before planning your departure-day meal here.

Name: FIG
Description: Seasonal, ingredient-focused cooking; a strong choice for your main occasion dinner. Menus change, so choose it for the cooking rather than one promised dish.
Planning notes: Book as soon as your date becomes available. Check the restaurant's own booking link for its release policy.

Name: Delaney Oyster House
Description: Oysters, raw-bar dishes and seafood in a historic house; convenient before a Gaillard performance or after Marion Square.
Planning notes: Reservations recommended. Published service includes dinner daily and lunch Friday–Sunday; verify the trip-week schedule.

Name: Hank's Seafood Restaurant
Description: Traditional Charleston seafood close to the City Market. A useful choice for a group that wants familiar seafood preparations and a substantial dinner.
Planning notes: Reserve. Published lunch is Thursday–Sunday, 11:30–2; dinner nightly from 5.

Name: 167 Raw Oyster Bar
Description: Lively seafood and oyster-bar stop on lower King Street. Convenient for lunch or an early dinner while shopping.
Planning notes: First come, first served; no reservations. Published Mon–Sat 11am–11pm, closed Sunday. Visit by Oct. 31; allow for a wait.

Name: Cru Café
Description: A small historic-house café with comfort food; an appealing lunch break near the market and Ansonborough.
Planning notes: Reserve when available. Confirm lunch and dinner operating days rather than assuming all-day service.

Name: Basic Kitchen
Description: Vegetable-forward bowls and seasonal plates. A useful lighter meal between richer Lowcountry dinners.
Planning notes: Review the current menu for dietary needs; the restaurant is not exclusively vegan.

Name: Le Farfalle
Description: Italian food and pasta, with a pleasant setting just off King. A good change of cuisine during a seafood-heavy trip.
Planning notes: Reserve dinner; request outdoor seating if offered, subject to weather.

Name: Poogan's Porch
Description: Southern cooking in a historic house. Choose it for biscuits, a substantial brunch or a classic Charleston dinner setting.
Planning notes: Published brunch daily 9–3; dinner 4:30–9:30. Reservations recommended, especially Halloween weekend.

Name: Husk
Description: Seasonal Southern cooking in a historic Queen Street house; an alternative occasion dinner to FIG.
Planning notes: Book ahead and read the day's menu. Restaurant and bar arrangements may differ.

Name: 82 Queen
Description: Lowcountry dishes and a courtyard setting; especially useful for she-crab soup and shrimp-and-grits seekers.
Planning notes: Reserve. Lunch weekdays, brunch weekends and dinner daily are currently advertised.

Name: Slightly North of Broad
Description: An established Lowcountry bistro on East Bay. Works well after the French Quarter or before an evening waterfront walk.
Planning notes: Reserve for dinner; lunch offers a convenient way to fit it into sightseeing.

Name: Fleet Landing
Description: Seafood with a harborfront setting. Prioritize this when you want water views with your meal.
Planning notes: Book ahead; outdoor seating and a specific view should not be assumed from a standard reservation.

Name: Halls Chophouse
Description: Steakhouse dinner or a substantial Sunday brunch. This is one of the higher-cost meal options near your base.
Planning notes: Reserve well ahead; business-casual attire is recommended. Published Sunday brunch 10–2.

Name: The Ordinary
Description: Seafood and oysters in a former bank building on Upper King; combine with a northbound shopping walk.
Planning notes: Dinner from 4, Wednesday–Monday. Reservations open 28 days ahead at noon per the venue; bar and patio also take walk-ins.

Name: The Darling Oyster Bar
Description: Oysters and seafood on Upper King; an option before Music Farm or after browsing the northern end of King Street.
Planning notes: Published Monday–Saturday from 4pm; Sunday from 11am. Reserve a dining table when offered.

Name: Indaco
Description: Italian cooking, pasta and wood-fired pizza; useful when the group wants an alternative to Southern food.
Planning notes: Reserve dinner, particularly Friday or Saturday.

Name: O-Ku
Description: Sushi and Japanese-inspired dishes close to Upper King nightlife.
Planning notes: Reserve a table and check the current menu; special rolls and prices change.

Name: Stella's
Description: Greek cooking and shareable plates a short detour west of King Street.
Planning notes: Reserve dinner; particularly useful for a group that enjoys sharing several dishes.

Name: Chez Nous
Description: An intimate restaurant with a very small daily-changing European menu, tucked into a residential court.
Planning notes: Check the day's menu before committing if anyone has strong dietary preferences. Published Tuesday–Sunday lunch and dinner.

Name: Chubby Fish
Description: Creative seafood in Elliotborough. A destination dinner that requires planning around its queue, not just its walking time.
Planning notes: No advance reservations for normal dining; published Tuesday–Saturday from 5. Closed Sunday, so not a Nov. 1 option.

Name: Xiao Bao Biscuit
Description: Asian-inspired shared dishes in a converted service station; a worthwhile longer walk for a change of pace.
Planning notes: Generally walk-in; published Monday–Saturday 11–10, closed Sunday. Read group-booking rules for a large party.

Name: Leon's Oyster Shop
Description: Fried chicken, oysters and a relaxed setting at the far end of a longer Upper King outing.
Planning notes: Published daily 11am–10pm. Reservations currently offered for groups of 6–12; smaller groups generally use walk-in seating. Longer-walk option.

Name: Caviar & Bananas
Description: A nearby café for coffee, breakfast, sandwiches and provisions. Particularly practical on arrival and departure days.
Planning notes: Published kitchen closes 3:30; espresso and ice cream continue to 6. Weekdays start 7, weekends 8.

Name: The Rise Coffee Bar
Description: Coffee and pastries at The Restoration, very close to your home base.
Planning notes: Published daily 7–5. A convenient quick breakfast when you have a timed museum or tour ticket.

Name: Kudu Coffee & Craft Beer
Description: Coffee, pastries and a courtyard, with craft beer later in the day. A natural stop near Marion Square.
Planning notes: The venue intentionally does not offer Wi-Fi; treat it as a place to relax rather than a work stop.

Name: Harken Café & Bakery
Description: Scratch-baked pastries, coffee, breakfast and lunch in the French Quarter area.
Planning notes: Published weekday 7–3, Saturday 8–3, Sunday 8–1. Sunday closes early, which matters on Nov. 1.

Name: Callie's Hot Little Biscuit — King Street
Description: Biscuit breakfast or a snack while heading up King Street. This listing is for the King Street shop, whose storefront is numbered 476½.
Planning notes: Expect a small space and possible breakfast lines. Confirm current hours; do not confuse it with the City Market location.

Name: Millers All Day
Description: Breakfast and brunch with a retro interior; works well before a South of Broad walk.
Planning notes: Despite the name, published downtown closing is 3 weekdays and 4 weekends. Opens 8; allow for a weekend wait.

Name: Carmella's Café & Dessert Bar
Description: Desserts, gelato, coffee and drinks, conveniently placed for an evening waterfront loop.
Planning notes: The Charleston page advertises daily 8am–midnight; verify late hours for your date.

Name: Off Track Ice Cream
Description: An ice-cream break just off King Street; easy to combine with shopping or Le Farfalle.
Planning notes: Published Sun–Thu noon–10pm, Fri–Sat noon–11pm. Check the current dairy-free flavors directly.

Name: Bitty & Beau's Coffee
Description: Coffee near the City Market, from a company known for employing people with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
Planning notes: Published daily 9–5; a useful mid-walk stop rather than an early breakfast.

Name: La Pâtisserie at Hotel Bennett
Description: French-style pastries and coffee at the north edge of Marion Square.
Planning notes: Published daily 7–8. Combine with the Saturday farmers market or Blue Bicycle Books.

Name: The Watch Rooftop
Description: One of the closest rooftop dining and drink options, above The Restoration.
Planning notes: Book for a meal; check weather and current service hours. Use the hotel entrance and ask for rooftop access.

Name: Citrus Club
Description: Rooftop drinks and broad city views at The Dewberry, convenient after Marion Square.
Planning notes: 21+. The hotel currently offers lunch reservations; other seating is first-come, first-served. Sunset is a popular time.

Name: The Living Room at The Dewberry
Description: An indoor hotel lounge suited to a quieter drink, especially when rooftop weather is poor.
Planning notes: Check current public service hours and seating availability at the hotel.

Name: Camellias
Description: Hotel Bennett's pink Champagne lounge, also offering a more formal afternoon tea experience.
Planning notes: Tea requires a reservation; standard bar service does not. Current tea calendar includes your Thursday–Sunday dates, subject to availability.

Name: Fiat Lux
Description: Hotel Bennett rooftop with city views and food. An alternative when you want a rooftop near Upper King.
Planning notes: Check weather and seating. Rooftop bar access does not imply access to the hotel's swimming pool.

Name: The Rooftop at The Vendue
Description: Rooftop drinks close to Waterfront Park; an easy final stop on a French Quarter evening.
Planning notes: Confirm access, age policy and current hours; an outdoor table depends on weather and capacity.

Name: The Gin Joint
Description: A cocktail-focused stop near the waterfront and French Quarter restaurants.
Planning notes: Allow for a wait in a small venue; check current booking/seating details.

Name: Proof
Description: A compact cocktail bar on Upper King, near Halls and Blue Bicycle Books.
Planning notes: Evening option; verify hours and allow flexibility around busy Friday/Saturday service.

Name: Blind Tiger Pub
Description: A pub and courtyard option on Broad Street, useful for a casual break on the way to or from the Battery.
Planning notes: Check food-service hours separately from bar closing time.

Name: Charleston City Market
Description: Historic market sheds with crafts, gifts and sweetgrass baskets. Walk the length toward East Bay, rather than stopping at the first building.
Planning notes: Day market opens 9:30; the site gives conflicting 5/5:30 closing times, so plan before 5. Friday/Saturday night market is separately advertised.

Name: Marion Square / Saturday farmers market
Description: A central green space and the Saturday farmers market location. Especially useful for a relaxed breakfast-and-browsing morning.
Planning notes: The published 2026 season covers Saturday Oct. 31, 8am–2pm. Check for weather or event changes that week.

Name: College of Charleston — Cistern Yard
Description: An attractive oak-shaded campus space with historic architecture, very close to Society Street.
Planning notes: Use public paths and respect classes or reserved events. Indoor buildings are not assumed open for tourism.

Name: Kahal Kadosh Beth Elohim
Description: Historic synagogue and an opportunity to learn about Charleston's Jewish community.
Planning notes: Consult the congregation's current tour schedule and visitor/security arrangements; worship times are not sightseeing slots.

Name: Gibbes Museum of Art
Description: American art with strong Charleston and Southern connections. A particularly useful indoor choice on a rainy day.
Planning notes: Check exhibition dates, admission and gallery hours directly; allow extra time if you enjoy art.

Name: The Charleston Museum
Description: A broad introduction to local history, natural history and material culture; a good orientation museum for a first visit.
Planning notes: Compare combination tickets if you also want Joseph Manigault or Heyward-Washington House.

Name: Joseph Manigault House
Description: A historic house visit that explores a wealthy rice-planting family's home and the enslaved people who lived and worked there.
Planning notes: Pair with The Charleston Museum across the street; verify guided-tour departure times.

Name: Aiken-Rhett House
Description: Preserved house, work spaces and enslaved people's quarters; a substantial architectural and social-history visit.
Planning notes: Published Tue–Sun admission 10–4, with visitors allowed to remain until 5. Compare the Nathaniel Russell combination ticket.

Name: International African American Museum
Description: A major museum on Gadsden's Wharf exploring African American history and connections across the African diaspora. Give this time rather than fitting it into a quick photo stop.
Planning notes: Book timed entry. Detailed visitor page: Tue–Sat 10–5; Sunday noon–5 from July 2026, last entry 4. Its header differs, so follow the booking calendar.

Name: South Carolina Aquarium
Description: South Carolina wildlife, marine habitats and sea turtle recovery exhibits. A strong option with children or in wet weather.
Planning notes: Check date-specific tickets and last entry; plan earlier in the day rather than close to closing.
Coordinate source: OpenStreetMap aquarium building bounds; approximate center

Name: Liberty Square / Fort Sumter Visitor Center
Description: Harborfront history stop and a departure area for Fort Sumter trips. The visitor center is walkable; the fort itself is on an island.
Planning notes: For a fort visit, book a separate ferry and confirm a downtown Liberty Square departure, not Patriots Point across the harbor.

Name: Waterfront Park / Pineapple Fountain
Description: Harbor views, the famous Pineapple Fountain and a pleasant place to sit between sightseeing stops.
Planning notes: Map pin marks the Vendue Range approach, not the fountain's exact position. Continue south through the park to the fountain.

Name: Rainbow Row
Description: The colorful historic houses along East Bay; best as part of a longer waterfront-to-Battery walk.
Planning notes: The pin marks the row's southern area; the houses extend along the block. They are private homes, viewed from the sidewalk.

Name: Old Slave Mart Museum
Description: A focused and sobering account of Charleston's domestic slave trade at a former auction site.
Planning notes: Plan a weekday or Saturday; verify operating hours. This is a separate site from the City Market.

Name: Old Exchange & Provost Dungeon
Description: Colonial and Revolutionary history in a prominent historic building, including the dungeon tour.
Planning notes: Published adults $16; Mon–Sat 9–5, Sunday 11–5. Recheck current ticket details before visiting.

Name: The Powder Magazine
Description: A compact colonial-history museum in a surviving early gunpowder store. Easy to fit between the market and Church Street.
Planning notes: Current site advertises Mon–Sat 10–5; do not rely on Sunday access.

Name: St. Philip's Church
Description: A distinctive church and streetscape in the French Quarter; combine with the Dock Street Theatre and Chalmers Street.
Planning notes: Check posted access for the church and churchyard. Services, weddings and preservation work can limit entry.

Name: St. Michael's Church
Description: Historic church at Broad and Meeting, a useful landmark on a South of Broad walk.
Planning notes: Exterior viewing is straightforward; verify visitor hours before expecting interior access.

Name: Circular Congregational Church
Description: A distinctive church and historic burial ground along the main museum corridor.
Planning notes: Observe posted churchyard hours and check the calendar for concerts; cemetery access is not assumed after dark.

Name: Washington Square
Description: A small green pause behind City Hall, convenient between Meeting Street museums and South of Broad.
Planning notes: Combine with the Four Corners of Law at Broad and Meeting; monuments are best understood with their historical context.

Name: Nathaniel Russell House
Description: A restored historic house with a notable staircase, interiors and interpretation of the enslaved people who supported the household.
Planning notes: Published Tue–Sun admission 10–4, stay until 5. Combine admission with Aiken-Rhett if you want contrasting house-museum experiences.

Name: Heyward-Washington House
Description: Revolutionary-era house, Charleston furniture and surviving work buildings; convenient on the way toward the Battery.
Planning notes: Compare the Charleston Museum's combination ticket and verify tour departures.

Name: Edmondston-Alston House
Description: A house museum on the harbor side of the Battery, useful when you want an interior visit during your southern walking loop.
Planning notes: Check current tour times and opening days; historic stairs may matter for accessibility.

Name: The Battery / East Battery promenade
Description: Harbor-edge walking past large historic houses. This is the classic southern extension of a Rainbow Row walk.
Planning notes: Map pin marks the southern end. Waterfront construction or weather may alter access; follow posted detours.

Name: White Point Garden
Description: Oaks, benches and monuments at the peninsula's southern tip. A natural rest stop before returning north.
Planning notes: Combine with East Battery; bring water because this residential end has fewer immediate café options.

Name: Colonial Lake
Description: A landscaped tidal lake with a perimeter path, west of the main tourist corridor. A good quieter walk or morning exercise option.
Planning notes: Pin marks an Ashley Avenue approach. Add time to circle the lake after reaching it.

Name: Cathedral of St. John the Baptist
Description: A Gothic Revival cathedral that pairs naturally with a westward Broad Street or Colonial Lake walk.
Planning notes: Check interior visitor access and service times; be respectful of worship in progress.

Name: Charleston City Gallery
Description: A gallery beside Waterfront Park, useful for adding contemporary art to a harbor stroll.
Planning notes: Exhibitions and opening days vary; confirm the current city listing before making it your main destination.

Name: Buxton Books
Description: Independent bookstore with local literary connections and events; well placed on lower King.
Planning notes: Check author-event dates and any associated tour departures separately.

Name: Blue Bicycle Books
Description: Used, rare and local books close to Marion Square and Halls.
Planning notes: Published Mon–Sat 10–7:30, Sunday 1–6. Not an early Sunday-morning stop.

Name: Croghan's Jewel Box
Description: Long-running family jeweler with estate pieces and Charleston-themed gifts.
Planning notes: Current official About page lists 155 King, despite older guides showing 308 King; use the newer address.

Name: Candlefish
Description: Candles, fragrance browsing and candle-making workshops, very convenient to your lodging.
Planning notes: Book workshops; the venue says finished candles are collected the next day. Avoid a last-day class unless pickup/shipping is arranged.

Name: Preservation Society Shop
Description: A useful stop for Charleston-related books and gifts; also connected with the society organizing the October Fall Tours.
Planning notes: The shop is not automatically the meeting point for a booked tour; follow the confirmation email.

Name: The Shops at The Charleston Place
Description: A cluster of higher-end retailers in and around a central hotel, useful for a short shopping break.
Planning notes: Use the current hotel directory; individual stores and access can change during renovations.

Name: Dock Street Theatre / Charleston Stage
Description: A historic theater in the French Quarter and home to Charleston Stage performances.
Planning notes: Broadway Bound runs Oct. 14–Nov. 1, 2026; Miss Nelson Is Missing! has an Oct. 31 family performance. Book the actual date/time and check content guidance; not every day in a production run has a performance.

Name: Theatre 99
Description: Improv comedy very close to Society Street; convenient if you want an evening activity without a long walk home.
Planning notes: Check the calendar and age guidance. Entrance is at the back, upstairs; a platform lift is available with staff assistance before the show.

Name: Charleston Gaillard Center
Description: Major performing-arts venue close to your lodging. Your dates include orchestral, author and piano events.
Planning notes: See the date-specific events section below and buy only for a time you can attend.

Name: Charleston Music Hall
Description: A downtown venue for music, comedy and other performances, near restaurants on Upper King.
Planning notes: Check the live event calendar; the venue's presence does not guarantee a show on every night of your stay.

Name: Music Farm
Description: A live-music venue near the visitor center, useful for an evening on the northern side of downtown.
Planning notes: Check each show's age restriction and standing/seating format. Under-18 guests must attend with an adult under current venue policy.

Name: Children's Museum of the Lowcountry
Description: Hands-on play and learning for families with younger children, near the Charleston Museum and visitor center.
Planning notes: Published Mon–Sat 10–5, Sunday noon–5. Check age suitability and current exhibits; mornings before 10 are member access.

Name: Bulldog Tours — downtown office
Description: A starting point for choosing ghost, history or food walks; a natural Halloween-period activity.
Planning notes: Office pin is not a guaranteed tour departure point. Book the specific tour and use its confirmation address; some offerings are across the harbor.

Name: Harris Teeter — East Bay Trading Station
Description: A full grocery option for breakfast supplies, water, snacks and food for your Airbnb.
Planning notes: Walking back with several bags takes longer; buy the heavy items in one planned run or consider delivery.

Name: Target — King Street
Description: Convenient for toiletries, snacks and forgotten basics while already on King Street.
Planning notes: This is a downtown store; selection may differ from a large suburban Target. Check trip-week hours.

Name: CVS — George Street
Description: A very close option for toiletries, over-the-counter basics and pharmacy services.
Planning notes: Retail, pharmacy and clinic hours are different; confirm the service you need directly.

Name: Charleston Visitor Center
Description: Visitor information and a useful orientation point near several museums and performance venues.
Planning notes: Ask for current walking maps, public-restroom locations and transit information; check daily opening hours.

Name: Christophe Chocolate
Description: Artisan chocolates and sweets just along your own street. One of the easiest stops for a treat or a gift to take home.
Planning notes: Check the downtown shop's current pastry selection and hours; allow careful packing for chocolate gifts.

Name: Handy & Hot
Description: Biscuits, hand pies, coffee and quick bites very close to your Airbnb.
Planning notes: A practical grab-and-go breakfast; check the current morning opening and kitchen closing times.

Name: Peninsula Grill — reopening to confirm
Description: A fine-dining option near the market, known for its coconut cake. Keep it as a conditional possibility rather than a firm plan.
Planning notes: IMPORTANT: official site currently says temporarily closed for renovation, reopening this fall, with no confirmed date shown. Verify reopening for your dates before planning around it.

Name: Verde — King Street
Description: Fast-casual salads, wraps and bowls near the northern end of your immediate neighborhood.
Planning notes: Useful for a quicker and lighter lunch; check current downtown opening hours and menu.

Name: CO — Charleston
Description: Asian-inspired noodles and other casual dishes on King Street, close enough for an uncomplicated meal near home.
Planning notes: Current location page says daily opening at 11am; check the menu and kitchen closing time.

Name: South Carolina Historical Society Museum
Description: State history told through objects, documents and interactive exhibits in the historic Fireproof Building beside Washington Square.
Planning notes: Published Tue–Sat 10–4; recommended last admission 3:15. Closed Sunday and Monday, so visit by Oct. 31.

Name: Charleston Library Society
Description: A historic private library on lower King, worth noticing while visiting Buxton Books and nearby shops.
Planning notes: Routine access is for members. The public can attend designated events with RSVP; do not plan on a walk-in reading-room visit.

Name: Mercantile & Mash
Description: A café and food stop in the Cigar Factory, with a separate bar component. A longer northeastern outing beyond the main visitor core.
Planning notes: Mercantile closes 5:30 weekdays, 4 Saturday, 3 Sunday. Bar Mash has separate hours and is closed Sunday.

Name: The Grocery
Description: Seasonal cooking with an emphasis on local produce, seafood and meat; a dinner destination just off Upper King.
Planning notes: Reserve dinner and confirm the current operating days.

Name: Church and Union Charleston
Description: Your requested addition: Modern American dining in a converted historic church, with a dramatic interior. Convenient for brunch, lunch or dinner around the City Market. The restaurant's full address is 32B North Market Street.
Planning notes: Reserve through the Charleston page's OpenTable link. Published dinner daily from 5; lunch Mon–Thu 10–3:30; brunch Fri–Sun 9–3:30; midday menu daily 3:30–5. For 12 or more, use the venue's group inquiry process. Phone: 843-937-8666.

Name: Vintage Lounge
Description: A relaxed Upper King wine bar focused on cocktails, wines by the glass, local beer, and a changing cheese and charcuterie selection.
Planning notes: Published hours are Wednesday–Sunday from 5pm; closed Monday and Tuesday. Check the current beverage and bottle lists before going.

Name: Cooper Coffee & Wine
Description: A sunlit waterfront café beside The Cooper Marina, serving coffee and breakfast before shifting to lunch; evening wine service is described as coming soon.
Planning notes: Published breakfast hours are 7–11am and lunch is 11am–4pm. Confirm whether evening wine service has begun before planning a later visit.
